kaps_punt: Handel as ruil van goedere; en Handel as die koop en verkoop van goedere vir geld

items.bewering: Niemand kan alles wat hy nodig het self maak, plant of myn nie.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Self-sustainability' (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-sustainability): full self-sufficiency is defined as a way of living 'in which nothing is consumed other than what is produced by the self-sufficient individuals', with homesteading and off-the-grid living as practised forms; it is called usually inefficient and rare, but not impossible. A Mises Institute lecture (mises.org, 'Economy, Society, and History', lecture 3) likewise says a person could produce everything alone and stay self-sufficient. No source I found supports the claim that it CANNOT be done. Wikipedia, 'Division of labour': 'The division of labour is the motive for trade and the source of economic interdependence' supports the lesson's actual point, that people in practice depend on others.
items.regstelling: The sentence says it is impossible for anyone to make, grow or mine everything they need ('Niemand kan ... nie'). That is an absolute that overstates. Self-sufficient living is rare and hard, but people have done it. Narrow the quantifier, not the point: for example, almost nobody makes everything they need themselves, or most people cannot. The lesson's reason for trade, that people specialise and then depend on one another, stays exactly as it is. The title 'Niemand maak alles self nie' carries the same absolute about practice rather than ability. In practice it holds far more closely, but the writer should decide whether the title matches the narrowed sentence.

items.bewering: 'n Boer plant mielies op sy plaas, maar hy maak nie self skoene nie.
items.bron: An illustrative scenario, not a claim about every farmer. It is consistent with Wikipedia, 'Division of labour' (specialisation is the motive for trade and the source of interdependence).

items.bewering: Baie mense maak of plant meestal een ding, meer as wat hulle nodig het. Van ander dinge het hulle te min.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Division of labour': people specialise and 'trade to take advantage of others' capabilities in addition to their own'. Introductory economics summaries (CliffsNotes study notes, 'Understanding Gains from Trade: The Power of Specialization') say that when people specialise 'they produce a surplus of their chosen goods or services. However, they still require other products they do not produce.' The quantifier 'baie mense ... meestal' is suitably careful.

items.bewering: Die boer het baie mielies, en die soutmaker by die soutpan het sout.
items.bron: In South Africa salt has been collected from pans for centuries. At Tswaing (the former Pretoria Zoutpan), Mail & Guardian, 'Salt of the earth' (1997), describes Tswana-speaking people processing the salt crust about 800 years ago. Visit Gauteng (gauteng.net) records Stone Age salt collection at the crater lake and later commercial salt production. The lesson names no particular pan and makes only the general claim.

items.bewering: Uit hierdie verskil tussen mense ontstaan handel.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Division of labour': 'The division of labour is the motive for trade and the source of economic interdependence.'

items.bewering: Die boer neem sy mielies na die soutmaker toe en kry sout terug.
items.bron: An illustrative barter scenario. It fits the definition of barter in Wikipedia, 'Barter' (directly trading goods for other goods without a medium of exchange).

items.bewering: Handel is wanneer mense goedere of dienste uitruil: deur te ruil, of deur te koop en te verkoop.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Trade': 'Trade is the act by which people take something of value (such as products, resources, money) in exchange', including goods or services exchanged for money. Britannica Money, 'Barter' (britannica.com/money/barter-trade, search snippet): barter is 'the oldest form of commerce', so it counts as a form of trade alongside buying and selling.

items.bewering: Ruilhandel is die naam vir hierdie direkte ruil sonder geld. Ruilhandel is een manier om handel te dryf en nie 'n ander naam vir handel nie.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Barter': 'an exchange system in which participants directly trade goods or services for other goods or services, without a medium of exchange such as money'. Britannica Money, 'Barter' (search snippet): direct trading of goods or services without money, 'the oldest form of commerce'. So barter is one form of trade, not a synonym for it.

items.bewering: Die soutmaker moet mielies wil hê op dieselfde dag dat die boer sout soek. Wil die soutmaker daardie dag iets anders hê, loop die boer met sy sak weg.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Barter', section on problems of barter: the double coincidence of wants requires each party to have what the other wants at the moment of exchange. The farmer-and-salt-maker scenario maps this correctly.

items.bewering: Baie goedere kan ook nie in kleiner stukke verdeel word nie. Jy kan nie 'n halwe bok vir 'n handvol sout aanbied nie.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Barter', on indivisibility: someone who holds only one indivisible item worth more than what they want cannot complete the trade; a cow is the classic case. Mapping check: a live goat cannot be halved without killing it, and a whole goat is worth far more than a handful of salt, so the example carries the concept correctly. A learner who reasons 'slaughter it, then' lands on meat, which spoils, and the next sentence covers exactly that problem, so the reasoning is not led astray.

items.bewering: Vis en melk bly ook nie lank goed nie en raak gou sleg.
items.bron: UC Agriculture and Natural Resources, UC Master Food Preservers of Central Sierra, 'Observe the 2-hour rule' (ucanr.edu): perishable foods, milk included, should not stand at room temperature for more than two hours; fresh fish is treated as highly perishable. Wikipedia, 'Barter': relying on perishable goods makes saving and later exchange impractical. This supports listing it as a difficulty of direct exchange.

items.bewering: Met geld hoef die koper en die verkoper nie meer presies by mekaar te pas nie. Die boer verkoop sy mielies aan enigeen wat mielies nodig het. Hy koop dan met daardie geld sout by 'n heel ander mens.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Barter', and introductory economics summaries (e.g. Pearson study notes, 'Unit 5 the monetary sector'): money as a medium of exchange removes the need for a double coincidence of wants, so a seller can sell to one person and buy from another.

items.bewering: Die blokvolgorde (ruil sonder geld, dan waar ruil moeilik raak, dan koop en verkoop met geld) en 'nie meer' in 'Met geld hoef ... nie meer presies by mekaar te pas nie'
items.bron: Checked as an implied picture. Wikipedia, 'Barter' (section on anthropology): no ethnographic study has found a society that used barter with no other medium of exchange, and anthropologists have found no evidence that money arose out of barter; Adam Smith's sequence was a hypothetical history. The lesson does NOT say that barter came first historically or that money was invented to replace it. It compares the two as ways of trading, and 'nie meer' refers to the same farmer's situation. As written, the mapping is a functional comparison and holds. Recorded so that no revision adds a historical 'first barter, then money was invented' sentence. That claim is disputed and should not be stated as fact.

items.bewering: Geld werk omdat die mense rondom jou dit as betaling aanvaar.
items.bron: Bank of England Quarterly Bulletin 2014 Q1, 'Money in the modern economy: an introduction': money is special 'because everyone in the economy trusts that it will be accepted by other people in exchange for goods and services'. Bank of England explainer 'Why does money depend on trust?'.

items.bewering: Die boer kan die geld ook hou tot hy iets anders nodig het.
items.bron: Store of value as a function of money: Pearson study notes, 'Unit 5 the monetary sector' (money 'retains value over time, allowing individuals to save purchasing power for future use'), and Wikipedia, 'Barter' (money as a store of wealth, against perishable goods). The South African Reserve Bank's mandate is to protect the value of the currency (resbank.co.za, 'The Reserve Bank and its functions').

items.bewering: Met geld betaal mense ook vir dienste, soos wanneer 'n haarkapper jou hare sny.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Trade': goods or services are exchanged for money. A haircut is a standard example of a service: the buyer gets a benefit and no ownership passes (Ferris State University, 'Definition of Goods and Services').

items.bewering: Mense ruil vandag nog goedere en dienste direk vir mekaar sonder geld.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Barter', modern use: barter returns wherever money is scarce, for example in Venezuela during hyperinflation and at Argentina's barter clubs in 1998-2002. Britannica Money, 'Barter' (search snippet): it is still common in traditional societies. Note for the writer: Bartercard, which operates in South Africa, uses an electronic 'trade dollar', so it is not direct barter and should not be cited as an example of it.

items.bewering: Mense koop en verkoop ook elke dag goedere met geld.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Trade': trade involves transferring goods or services in exchange for money. This is the ordinary daily form of trade.

items.bewering: Handel begin nie by geld nie maar by iets wat iemand nodig het.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Division of labour': the division of labour, which means needing what others make, 'is the motive for trade'. This is a statement about motive, not about history, and is consistent with the anthropological evidence recorded above.

items.bewering: Handel is wanneer mense goedere of dienste uitruil: deur te ruil, of deur te koop en te verkoop.
items.bron: Same as the identical sentence in 'Ruil sonder geld': Wikipedia, 'Trade'; Britannica Money, 'Barter'. The entry is the same sentence as the study text, so the two cannot drift.

items.bewering: Ruilhandel is wanneer mense goedere of dienste direk vir mekaar ruil sonder geld.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Barter': participants 'directly trade goods or services for other goods or services, without a medium of exchange such as money'.

items.bewering: Goedere is dinge wat mense ruil, koop of verkoop, soos mielies of skoene.
items.bron: Ferris State University, 'Definition of Goods and Services': goods are items whose ownership passes completely to the buyer. Vedantu, 'Difference between goods and services': goods are tangible and can be kept. Maize and shoes are tangible goods. The entry also reads correctly on its own.

items.bewering: 'n Diens is werk wat iemand vir 'n ander doen, sodat die ander die werk self kry en nie 'n ding wat hy of sy kan hou nie.
items.bron: Ferris State University, 'Definition of Goods and Services': with a service 'ownership does not transfer to the purchaser, but the purchaser benefits in some way'. Inflibnet e-PG Pathshala, 'Goods vs. Service Marketing': services cannot be stored and are produced and consumed at the same time. The definition is accurate as well as simple.

opsomming: One claim must be narrowed: 'Niemand kan alles wat hy nodig het self maak, plant of myn nie' says self-sufficiency is impossible, but sources describe it as rare and hard, not impossible. 'Byna niemand' or 'die meeste mense kan nie' fixes it, and the title should be checked against the narrowed sentence. Everything else holds, including the barter problems and the functions of money. The lesson rightly never says that money was invented to replace barter, which anthropologists dispute, and no revision should add that.
